wolf_spider.name: Wolf Spider
wolf_spider.guide: Eight eyes, eight legs, zero manners. She doesn't build webs because she'd rather chase you personally.

ground_beetle.name: Ground Beetle
ground_beetle.guide: A shiny black tank that patrols the lawn at night. Will steal your crumbs and your dignity.

dead_beetle.name: Dead Beetle
dead_beetle.guide: The finest beetle in the yard: motionless, delicious and only slightly smelly. Bring friends to carry it.

robin.name: Robin
robin.guide: Humans put it on greeting cards. We put it on our list of reasons to stay underground.

earthworm.name: Earthworm
earthworm.guide: A pink tunnel-boring machine that eats dirt and ruins architecture. Harmless, enormous, and full of protein.

aphid.name: Aphid
aphid.guide: A tiny green sugar fountain on legs. Tickle it with an antenna and it pays you in honeydew.

rhino_beetle.name: Rhinoceros Beetle
rhino_beetle.guide: Can lift 850 times its own weight, and is surprisingly happy to let a dozen ants ride on its horn.

house_cat.name: House Cat
house_cat.guide: A furry god of boredom. It is not hungry; it simply wants to see what happens when it pats you.

homeowner.name: Homeowner
homeowner.guide: A mountain that wears slippers. Mostly harmless until it notices the trail to the sugar bowl.

exterminator.name: Exterminator
exterminator.guide: Arrives in a van with a picture of a sad ant on it. We do not find this funny.

rival_worker.name: Red Ant Worker
rival_worker.guide: Lives under the garden gnome, smells of vinegar and arrogance. Bites first, asks questions never.

queen_ant.name: Our Queen
queen_ant.guide: Mother of all of us, quite literally. She lays eggs, gives orders, and has not seen daylight since her wedding.

woodlouse.name: Woodlouse
woodlouse.guide: A tiny armoured armadillo that breathes through its legs. Technically a lobster that got lost.

pill_bug.name: Pill Woodlouse
pill_bug.guide: Rolls into a perfect ball when threatened. We roll it home anyway.

garden_snail.name: Garden Snail
garden_snail.guide: Carries its house on its back, which seems like a lot of effort when you could just dig one.

slug.name: Grey Field Slug
slug.guide: A snail that sold its house. Leaves a slime trail that confuses our scent trails terribly.

ladybird.name: Seven-spot Ladybird
ladybird.guide: Adorable to humans, a menace to our aphid herds. Each spot is one more reason to bite it.

honeybee.name: Honeybee
honeybee.guide: Our distant cousin who moved to the sky and got into the honey business. Stings, then regrets it forever.

bumblebee.name: Bumblebee
bumblebee.guide: A flying fluffball that, according to old science, should not be able to fly. Nobody told it.

wasp.name: Common Wasp
wasp.guide: A bee that chose violence. In late summer it gets drunk on fallen fruit and picks fights.

hoverfly.name: Hoverfly
hoverfly.guide: Dresses up as a wasp to look tough. Up close it's a total sweetheart that just hangs in the air.

housefly.name: Housefly
housefly.guide: Tastes with its feet and walks on our food. When it lands dead, it is the perfect snack.

dead_fly.name: Dead Fly
dead_fly.guide: Lying on its back, legs in the air, looking terribly dramatic. Two ants can carry it home.

mosquito.name: Mosquito
mosquito.guide: Wants blood but we're too small to bother with. The only thing in the yard humans hate more than us.

cabbage_white.name: Cabbage White
cabbage_white.guide: A floating napkin with ambitions. Its caterpillars are a buffet waiting to happen.

caterpillar.name: Cabbage Caterpillar
caterpillar.guide: A green sausage that only eats leaves and never says thank you. Soft, slow and very welcome at dinner.

moth.name: Large Yellow Underwing
moth.guide: Flies into the porch light over and over, convinced this time will be different.

centipede.name: Brown Centipede
centipede.guide: Fifteen pairs of legs and a pair of venom fangs. Not one of those legs has ever been used for good.

millipede.name: Black Snake Millipede
millipede.guide: Has hundreds of legs and no idea where any of them are. Smells awful when poked; we've checked.

earwig.name: Common Earwig
earwig.guide: Waves its bottom pincers like it means business. It mostly means it wants to hide in a flowerpot.

field_cricket.name: Field Cricket
field_cricket.guide: Sings all night by rubbing its wings together. We would sleep, if ants slept.

grasshopper.name: Meadow Grasshopper
grasshopper.guide: Moves in great leaps for no reason. Somewhere out there, it is still jumping.

harvestman.name: Harvestman
harvestman.guide: A pea balanced on eight drinking straws. Not a spider, and very tired of being told it is.

garden_spider.name: Garden Spider
garden_spider.guide: Builds a beautiful wheel of silk and waits. Admire it from a very long way away.

money_spider.name: Money Spider
money_spider.guide: Smaller than our head. Humans think it brings luck; to us it brings a snack.

springtail.name: Springtail
springtail.guide: Has a spring under its tummy and launches itself away whenever we get close. Rude.

lacewing.name: Green Lacewing
lacewing.guide: Looks like a fairy. Its larvae eat aphids by the hundred. Fairies can be monsters.

leafhopper.name: Leafhopper
leafhopper.guide: A tiny green rocket that sips plant juice. Blink and it has teleported to another leaf.

froghopper.name: Froghopper
froghopper.guide: Its children live in bubbles of spit. Humans call it cuckoo spit; we call it a hard pass.

shield_bug.name: Green Shield Bug
shield_bug.guide: Shaped like a medieval shield and smells like a medieval moat when bothered.

vine_weevil.name: Vine Weevil
vine_weevil.guide: A beetle with an elephant's nose. It plays dead when touched, which saves us a step.

rove_beetle.name: Devil's Coach-horse
rove_beetle.guide: Raises its tail like a scorpion and opens its jaws wide. Sounds like a pub name, acts like a bouncer.

click_beetle.name: Click Beetle
click_beetle.guide: When flipped on its back it snaps itself into the air with a loud click. Show-off.

dung_beetle.name: Dor Beetle
dung_beetle.guide: Spends its life rolling and burying the yard's least loved resource. A true hero.

stag_beetle.name: Stag Beetle
stag_beetle.guide: Huge antler-jaws used only for wrestling other stag beetles. Impressively useless, like most romance.

crane_fly.name: Crane Fly
crane_fly.guide: Daddy-long-legs: drops a leg every time it panics, which is always.

damselfly.name: Azure Damselfly
damselfly.guide: A blue needle that hovers near the birdbath. Too elegant to notice us, which suits us fine.

thrips.name: Thrips
thrips.guide: One thrips, two thrips, still thrips. The only creature smaller and more numerous than us.

red_velvet_mite.name: Red Velvet Mite
red_velvet_mite.guide: A walking red velvet cushion. Tastes terrible, which is probably why it can afford to be that colour.

tick.name: Castor Bean Tick
tick.guide: Waits on a grass blade for something warm to walk past. We are not warm. It is disappointed.

mite.name: Soil Mite
mite.guide: A crumb with legs that lives in our walls. Eats mould, so we let it stay. Mostly.

blackbird.name: Blackbird
blackbird.guide: Hops across the lawn listening for worms. Hears us too. Run.

sparrow.name: House Sparrow
sparrow.guide: Chirpy, brown and always in a gang. Eats crumbs, seeds and, on bad days, ants.

frog.name: Common Frog
frog.guide: Has a tongue faster than our reflexes. Thankfully it prefers flies that hold still.

toad.name: Common Toad
toad.guide: A grumpy lump of warts that lives under the shed. Antonia says it ate her cousin. Antonia says a lot.

hedgehog.name: Hedgehog
hedgehog.guide: A pincushion that snuffles through the flowerbeds at night eating beetles. We approve of half of that.

mouse.name: House Mouse
mouse.guide: Lives behind the skirting board and steals the same crumbs we do. Professional rival, personal friend.

wireworm.name: Wireworm
wireworm.guide: A click beetle's child that chews through roots and tunnels. Teenagers, honestly.

leatherjacket.name: Leatherjacket
leatherjacket.guide: The crane fly's grub: a tough grey bag that eats grass roots and blunders into our tunnels.

chafer_grub.name: Chafer Grub
chafer_grub.guide: A curled-up white grub the size of a palace. Digs slowly, eats roots, and never apologises.

pot_worm.name: Pot Worm
pot_worm.guide: A tiny white thread that wiggles through damp soil. Shows up wherever we get careless with the midden.

nematode.name: Nematode
nematode.guide: There are more of these in a handful of soil than ants in the colony. Thankfully they mind their own business.

mole_cricket.name: Mole Cricket
mole_cricket.guide: Half cricket, half mole, all trouble. Has shovels for hands and dreams of our tunnels.

silverfish.name: Silverfish
silverfish.guide: A shiny fish-shaped thing that eats wallpaper glue and book bindings. Very literary.

cockroach.name: German Cockroach
cockroach.guide: Will survive the end of the world, and in the meantime it wants your sugar. Fight it for every grain.

dust_mite.name: Dust Mite
dust_mite.guide: Lives in the carpet and eats human skin flakes. Gross, even by our standards, and we live in dirt.

fruit_fly.name: Fruit Fly
fruit_fly.guide: Appears by magic around the fruit bowl. Scientists love it; it loves the bin.

bed_bug.name: Bed Bug
bed_bug.guide: The homeowner's least favourite lodger. Nobody has ever been happy to meet one, us included.

house_spider.name: House Spider
house_spider.guide: Sprints across the carpet in autumn looking for love. Will settle for an ant.

booklouse.name: Booklouse
booklouse.guide: Lives in old books, eats mould and has never finished a single chapter.

clothes_moth.name: Clothes Moth
clothes_moth.guide: Has eaten holes in every jumper in the wardrobe. We respect the commitment.

carpet_beetle.name: Varied Carpet Beetle
carpet_beetle.guide: Looks like a speckled pebble. Its fuzzy children eat the carpet one fibre at a time.

drain_fly.name: Drain Fly
drain_fly.guide: A fuzzy heart-shaped fly that lives in the plughole. The kitchen sink is its kingdom.
